analysis.title: PrimeView (Recap): Thursday Broadly Risk Off; Pain Driven by AI Beta, Only 7th Lgst Degross
key_insights: Thursday's US tech sell-off was the largest since Covid, but hedge fund flows were not the main driver. HF sells outweighed buys almost 6x and HFs cut 1.1std of US gross, only the 7th largest degross day since 1 Oct. Comparison days: Oct 28 at -2.3std, Oct 29 at -2.1std, Oct 21 at -2.2std.
The US selling came more from broader AI-related beta (macro, trend-following systematics, retail) than from equity L/S managers cutting favoured single-stock trades.

Attribution shows hedge funds made money on relative trades within pockets (Neoclouds, Optical & Networking) even though the overall baskets fell sharply. This matches October's shift from broad long selling to relative-value stock picking within baskets.
Estimated US performance on Thursday: Equity L/S managers +27bps, quants -49bps. The crowded L-S trade was up 2.5% at its intraday peak and closed up 1.2%.
US selling was concentrated in crowded AI Winners (-1.1std), Crowded Longs (-0.9std) and Hyperscalers (-1.2std). Semis long selling was moderate at -0.4std.

Flows were muted in Memory names despite a -16.6% move, and also muted in Hardware. UBS attributes this to hedge funds having de-risked the AI value chain since the summer and now focusing on single-stock relative value within AI. The most liquid names were cut rather than the most crowded, consistent with UBS's earlier deleveraging analysis.
Buy flow in the US was weak. US Pharma was the most bought group at +2std, but only +13bps on an absolute basis.
In Europe, hedge fund flows skewed to buying at +0.9std, concentrated in dip-buying in Banks (+2.6std) and Autos (+3.0std).
Intraday in Europe, Reinsurance is down significantly, but crowded longs are outperforming shorts in Reinsurance by 2.5% (crowding t-stat of 12). L-S holders in Airlines are down 76bps (t-stat 3.7).
Quant strategies lost money globally on Thursday.
US week-to-date: hedge funds de-risked High Momentum by -0.4std, with Crowded Longs de-risked similarly. They took profits of -1.8std in US Materials.
AI Resilient and AI Geared Software were the most bought US segment this week at +0.8std. Hedge funds have bought heavily since September as the Software vs. Semis negative correlation held.
In Europe this week, hedge funds de-risked Crowded Longs by -0.9std, concentrated in Quality names (-1.2std). EU Energy exposure fell a further -2.5std, and Renewables were sold down another -1.7std.
Renewables remain a UBS Equity Strategy and UBS Macro Equity Strategy top pick, with longs in ENGIE and Iberdrola.

Japan: hedge funds were net sellers at -110bps week-to-date, driven by de-risking into the US midterm elections. The UBS Deleveraging Indicator for Japan equity L/S switched on at the start of the week and remains on. The quant indicator is off.

In Japan, Consumer Discretionary was the most bought sector, net bought every day this week for +50bps WTD, as investors rotated into rate-sensitive and value consumer trades away from the AI trade. Info Tech was the most sold, at -1.7% WTD, on the broad AI unwind.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge funds were not the driver. Equity L/S managers made money on relative trades within AI pockets (Neoclouds, Optical & Networking), they had already de-risked the AI value chain since the summer, and the crowded L-S trade closed up 1.2%.
tension_points.bear_case: Broader AI beta selling by macro, trend-following systematics and retail drove the largest tech sell-off since Covid, with AI Winners at -1.1std, Hyperscalers at -1.2std and Memory names down -16.6%. Quants lost 49bps.
